elevator_state.controls: No elevator call panel, switch, intercom, or wall plate is visible.

movement_and_likely_before_after.movement: Only the woman has a travel cue: a lifted trailing foot and curved motion marks show left-to-right movement from the elevator side toward the apartment door. The man has no travel cue and appears stationary at the lever.
movement_and_likely_before_after.blind_most_likely_read: A woman has crossed from the elevator side to join a man at a closed apartment door; she presses the door while he tests the handle.
movement_and_likely_before_after.before_departure_readability: Not visually locked. A before-departure return is supported by her left-to-right path and his stationary position, but the still does not show her earlier movement toward the elevator or establish that the outing has not happened yet.
movement_and_likely_before_after.competing_arrival_read: Arrival remains plausible because she carries a tote and umbrella, approaches the apartment door from a fully closed elevator, and the man can read as testing or opening the door after they have returned.

uncertainties: A single still cannot prove that the man checked the lock twice; it shows one ongoing handle test.
The woman's precise gaze target is the man/door area rather than unequivocally her palm.
The exact before-departure chronology cannot be recovered image-first because the elevator is fully closed and the same blocking supports arrival.

semantic_verdict.summary: The creator-rejected central-lock defect is genuinely fixed: left hinges, a short-backset right-edge lever, plausible waist height, same-door palm contact, a fully closed exterior threshold, separate bodies, clean text, and woman-only movement all read correctly. The proof still fails the strict visual event because the elevator reads fully closed rather than visibly about 80 percent closed, and the image-first chronology cannot distinguish a before-departure return from arrival after an outing.
semantic_verdict.primary_failure: The nearly-closed elevator state and before-departure temporal phase are not visibly encoded strongly enough to eliminate the arrival reading.
